module


public import Mathlib.Order.Filter.Cofinite
public import Mathlib.Order.Interval.Finset.Defs
public import Mathlib.Order.SuccPred.Basic

@[expose] public section

open Set

namespace Filter

lemma cofinite_hasBasis_Ioi {α : Type*} [LinearOrder α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α] [OrderBot α] :
    cofinite.HasBasis (fun (_ : α) ↦ True) (Set.Ioi ·) := by
  constructor
  intro A
  simp only [mem_cofinite, true_and]
  constructor
  · intro hA
    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := Set.Finite.bddAbove hA
    use a
    rw [← Set.compl_subset_compl, compl_Ioi]
    exact ha
  · rintro ⟨a, ha⟩
    rw [← Set.compl_subset_compl, compl_Ioi] at ha
    apply Set.Finite.subset _ ha
    exact finite_Iic a

/--
Note(csonne): According to a TODO in `Mathlib.Order.Interval.Finset.Defs`, Assuming `SuccOrder α`
should not be necessary as an instance should follow from `[LocallyFiniteOrder α] [OrderBot α]`.
This has not been implemented in mathlib however.
-/
lemma cofinite_hasBasis_Ici {α : Type*} [LinearOrder α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α] [OrderBot α]
    [SuccOrder α] [NoMaxOrder α] : cofinite.HasBasis (fun (_ : α) ↦ True) (Set.Ici ·) := by
  constructor
  intro A
  simp only [mem_cofinite, true_and]
  constructor
  · intro hA
    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := Set.Finite.bddAbove hA
    use Order.succ a
    rw [← Set.compl_subset_compl, compl_Ici]
    exact Set.Subset.trans ha (Order.Iic_subset_Iio_succ a)
  · rintro ⟨a, ha⟩
    rw [← Set.compl_subset_compl, compl_Ici] at ha
    apply Set.Finite.subset _ ha
    exact finite_Iio a

theorem cofinite_eq_atTop {α : Type*} [LinearOrder α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α] [OrderBot α]
  [SuccOrder α] [NoMaxOrder α] :
    @cofinite α = atTop := by
  simp only [atTop_eq_generate_Ici, HasBasis.eq_generate cofinite_hasBasis_Ici, true_and]
  rfl

end Filter

findings.description: The note at lines 46–48 attributes the explicit `SuccOrder α` hypothesis to the construction not having been implemented in Mathlib. Mathlib already provides `LinearLocallyFiniteOrder.succOrder α`, which constructs this structure from `[LinearOrder α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α]`, even without `OrderBot`. What is absent is automatic instance registration, deliberately—not the mathematical construction. The lemma's statement and proof are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: Checked-out Mathlib, `Mathlib/Order/SuccPred/LinearLocallyFinite.lean`, lines 147–156: `noncomputable def succOrder [LocallyFiniteOrder ι] : SuccOrder ι`, in a context with `[LinearOrder ι]`. Its docstring explicitly explains: "This is not an instance, because its `succ` field conflicts with computable `SuccOrder` structures on `ℕ` and `ℤ`." A scratch Lean proof successfully installs this constructor locally and applies `Filter.cofinite_eq_atTop` without an assumed successor structure.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the unimplemented/TODO explanation with a reference to `LinearLocallyFiniteOrder.succOrder`, explaining that it is deliberately not registered as a global instance and can be installed locally after importing `Mathlib.Order.SuccPred.LinearLocallyFinite`. No mathematical statement change is required.

reformulations.difference: The closed-tail characterization explicitly takes a `SuccOrder α` structure, although that structure follows mathematically from the linear-order and local-finiteness hypotheses.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `LinearLocallyFiniteOrder.succOrder α` supplies such a structure. The HasBasis conclusion does not depend on the chosen successor, so universally quantifying over successor structures is equivalent to stating the conclusion without that parameter. The explicit parameter therefore excludes no intended mathematical orders. This equivalence was proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The equality explicitly takes a `SuccOrder α` structure in addition to linearity, local finiteness, a bottom element, and no maximum.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A successor structure can always be constructed from the existing linearity and local-finiteness assumptions. Neither cofinite nor atTop depends on that structure. The scratch file proves the equivalence between the successor-parameterized equality and the equality without that parameter, and proves the latter by installing Mathlib's constructor.
